title: IUD insertion
what: A gynecologist puts a small, flexible device into your womb to prevent pregnancy. There are copper IUDs and hormonal IUDs.
why: For long-lasting, reliable protection against pregnancy. A hormonal IUD is sometimes also used for heavy periods.
duration: the insertion itself usually takes 5 to 10 minutes; the whole visit about 30 minutes
tell_doctor: The date your last period started
If you had unprotected sex since your last period
Infections, discharge, or pain low in the belly
Allergy to copper or to medicines
If you had a C-section or surgery on your womb

prepare.title: Tests
prepare.text: Usually before insertion: an exam, swabs for infections, and sometimes an ultrasound. Your doctor will give you the list.

prepare.title: Day of your cycle
prepare.text: It is often put in during your period or right after. Other days are possible if pregnancy is ruled out. Ask your doctor.

prepare.title: Pain relief
prepare.text: Ask your doctor if you can take a painkiller about an hour before.

prepare.title: Food
prepare.text: Eat before your visit. On an empty stomach you may feel dizzy.

bring: The IUD, if your clinic asked you to buy it ahead of time
steps: You sit on the gynecology chair, and the doctor examines you
A speculum is put in, and the cervix is cleaned with antiseptic
The cervix is gently held in place with an instrument
A thin probe measures the depth of the womb
The IUD goes in through a thin tube and opens up inside
The IUD strings are trimmed. They stay in the vagina
feel: A feeling of pressure from the speculum
A few strong cramps, like painful period cramps. They last seconds
Sometimes weakness or dizziness. Lie down for a few minutes
after: Cramps and light spotting for a few days are normal
Sex and tampons: usually after a few days. Your doctor will tell you when
A follow-up check: usually after 4 to 6 weeks, or after your first period
Learn to check the strings after your period. Your doctor will show you how
red_flags: Severe pain low in the belly that does not go away with a painkiller
A fever above 38 degrees, or discharge with a bad smell
You cannot feel the strings, or you can feel the hard end of the IUD
Signs of pregnancy: see a gynecologist right away

faq.a: Usually there are a few strong cramps for seconds. Many people find it like painful period cramps. Tell your doctor if you are afraid of pain.

faq.q: When does an IUD start to protect me?
faq.a: A copper IUD, right away. A hormonal IUD, right away or after 7 days, depending on the day of your cycle. Ask your doctor.
Sometimes, yes, most often in the first months. That is why it is important to check the strings and go to your follow-up check.

reminders.text: IUD insertion tomorrow. Bring pads and your swab results. Eat before your visit.
